tasks.title: Gmail auth plumbing in health.py: env keys, token refresh, check_gmail, known_sources
tasks.notes: Research §1,§2,§6. GMAIL_SCOPE=gmail.readonly only. Regex ^GMAIL_([A-Z0-9]+)_REFRESH_TOKEN$ must not match GMAIL_CLIENT_ID/SECRET. gmail_accounts() mirrors slack_workspaces(): lowercased labels, sorted, empty value -> None. gmail_token_response(label) mirrors zoom_token_response(): plain POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token (client_id, client_secret, grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token); refresh returns NO new refresh token so nothing is written back. invalid_grant raises GmailAuthError (hard, never retried). check_gmail: refresh -> assert granted scope (space-delimited 'scope' field) contains gmail.readonly -> GET gmail/v1/users/me/profile (1 quota unit). invalid_grant message must name the likely causes (consent screen still in Testing = 7-day expiry, Google password change, revoked access) and 'auth/gmail_bootstrap.py <label>'. known_sources order: m365..., zoom, slack..., gmail.... Add GMAIL_ to the _env() prefix filter AND to tests/conftest.py CONFIG_PREFIXES. Tests stub requests.post/get at the health module, following tests/test_health.py.

tasks.title: runner._active() reuses known_sources() instead of a duplicated source list
tasks.notes: Research §7: runner.py:134-137 hand-copies the declared-source list, so a new source is silently never collected. Replace with known_sources(), drop the now-unused m365_aliases/slack_workspaces imports, update the source-id comments in db.py (SourceHealth, CollectedItem) to include gmail_<label>. Test: with a gmail account declared and toggled on, _active(config) contains gmail_<label>; toggled off, it does not.

tasks.title: Gmail transport: epoch-window list, page drain, quota-aware backoff
tasks.notes: Research §4,§5. messages.list q='after:<epoch_s> before:<epoch_s>' (NEVER date strings: they are PST-midnight), maxResults=500, drain every nextPageToken, raise at MAX_PAGES like graph.py rather than truncate. Convert the naive-UTC window to epoch with an explicit UTC tz (naive .timestamp() reads LOCAL time; see test_slack_oldest_is_utc_not_local) and pin it with a test under a non-UTC TZ. _call(): retry with truncated exponential backoff min(2**n + jitter, 32) on 403 with reason rateLimitExceeded/userRateLimitExceeded, on 429, and on 500/502/503/504; bounded attempts; 401 and other 4xx raise GmailError. Sleep via a module-level indirection so tests do not wait. Use plain requests.get (module-level, monkeypatched like graph/slack tests), NOT a Session and NOT parallel calls (deviation from research sketch: keeps the existing route() test helper valid). NO /batch, NO history.list, NO watch. Add test_gmail_* tests to tests/test_collectors.py.

tasks.title: Gmail message fetch and MIME flattening into a compact payload
tasks.notes: Research §4, §7 payload shape. messages.get format=full (20 quota units), sequential and paced (300 gets = the full 6,000 units/min/user budget). Decode base64url with padding fix; walk payload.parts recursively; prefer text/plain, else text/html stripped via stdlib html.parser dropping script/style AND hidden content (display:none, hidden attr, aria-hidden) since hidden HTML is a documented injection vector; charset from the part Content-Type, fallback utf-8 errors=replace. flatten_message() returns top-level keys: subject, from, to, cc, date, messageId, inReplyTo, listUnsubscribe, threadId, labelIds, snippet, internalDate, bodyText (capped, BODY_CAP default 20000 chars, a guess to be re-tuned from the dry run), bodyTruncated, attachments[{filename,mimeType,size}] (metadata only; never call attachments.get). 'subject' MUST be top-level so pipeline.collect PREVIEW_FIELDS shows it. internalDate (ms epoch string) -> naive UTC; unparseable -> None. Fixture tests/fixtures/gmail_message_multipart.json is SYNTHETIC (public repo: no real mail, names, or addresses) and is reused by T-009/T-013.

Item('mail', message id, occurred_at, payload). dispatch(): add 'gmail_' branch with a local import and gmail_accounts().get(label), like slack. tasks.title: auth/gmail_bootstrap.py: loopback + PKCE sign-in that prints the refresh token

runs.tail:
usage: gmail_bootstrap.py [-h] [--force] [--port PORT] [--no-browser] label

Interactive (browser, loopback + PKCE) sign-in for one Gmail label

positional arguments:
  label         mailbox label, letters/digits only, e.g. personal; becomes
                GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN

options:
  -h, --help    show this help message and exit
  --force       mint a new token even if the configured one is healthy
  --port PORT   loopback port to listen on (default: random free port)
  --no-browser  print the URL instead of opening a browser

tasks.notes: Research §1. Desktop OAuth client, auth-code + PKCE (S256), redirect http://127.0.0.1:<random port>, access_type=offline, prompt=consent, scope=GMAIL_SCOPE only. Stdlib http.server + secrets/hashlib + requests: NO google-auth-oauthlib dependency. Validate the state param; exchange the code (send client_secret); refuse to continue if the response has no refresh_token or the granted 'scope' lacks gmail.readonly; print the GMAIL_<LABEL>_REFRESH_TOKEN=... line for the user to paste into .env (never write it to a file). Short-circuit like m365_bootstrap.py: if a token is already configured and check_gmail is ok and not --force, exit 0. Support --port N and --no-browser (print the URL) so the loopback port can be SSH-forwarded from a headless box; that is an implementation note, not a documented Google recipe. Warn that every bootstrap run mints a token and Google keeps only 100 per client (oldest silently invalidated), so do not re-run casually. Unit-test the pure helpers (PKCE pair, URL builder, state check, scope assertion); the browser flow itself is a manual step.

tasks.title: NormalizedItem schema and Gmail adapter (pure function)
tasks.notes: Research §8 Q5: PROPOSAL, not sourced. Pydantic NormalizedItem: id (source:external_id), source, kind, occurred_at, title, body_text, body_truncated, participants[{name,address,role}], thread_key (gmail:<threadId>), labels, direction (inbound|outbound, from SENT label), is_unread, attachments (metadata), trust='untrusted_third_party', raw_ref, permalink=None (a Gmail URL format that works across accounts is unverified; deferred to the render phase). normalize_gmail() is a pure function over a CollectedItem-shaped input; add a dispatcher by source prefix that raises for sources without an adapter yet. Address parsing via email.utils.getaddresses. Include a deterministic strip_quoted_reply(text) and truncate(text, cap) helper. Tests feed the REAL output of flatten_message() from the T-005 fixture through the adapter, not a hand-built payload, so the two cannot drift.

tasks.title: Triage schema, alias mapping, output validation, deterministic stub fallback
tasks.notes: Research §8 Q1,Q3,Q4: pure logic, no SDK import yet. TriageRecord/TriageBatch Pydantic models with model_config extra='forbid'; categories and importance are string ENUMS (structured outputs reject numeric min/max and string length constraints, so ranges and lengths are enforced in Python post-parse). assign_aliases() gives per-run short ids (m001...) mapped to real ids in a dict: the model never sees or echoes real ids. batches(items, size~20). validate_batch(): every returned alias must be in the input set (unknown -> dropped), every input alias must be present (missing -> returned for one retry). sanitize_text(): strips URLs and markup and caps length (the model never emits URLs; links come from our own id->permalink map later). stub_record(item): deterministic record from subject/sender so a failed call degrades to a partial digest, never a dead run.

Add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SIGNALSLATE_MAP_MODEL to health._SINGLE_KEYS and tests/conftest.py CONFIG_KEYS so .env reaches the process the same way the other settings do (the SDK reads os.environ only, and locally .env is not loaded into it), plus a small llm_settings() accessor that returns the key and the model id. tasks.title: Map call: request builder, triage_items(), retry-then-stub degradation
tasks.notes: Research §8 Q1,Q4. build_request() returns the kwargs for client.messages.parse: system prompt with an <untrusted_content_policy> block, ONE user turn whose content is json.dumps of the batch (JSON escaping is the delimiter: a body containing </document> must not break out), the Pydantic model as the structured-output format, max_tokens set, and NO tools, NO network, NO temperature/top_p/top_k (400s on 4.7+ models; the SDK removes them). Find the correct structured-output kwarg name by inspecting the INSTALLED SDK (inspect.signature of anthropic.resources.messages.Messages.parse); do not guess it from prose docs. Contract test: every key build_request() emits must be a real parameter of that signature, so a stub client cannot hide a wrong kwarg. triage_items(items, client, model, batch_size) -> result with records, failures, stubbed ids: validate each batch, retry missing aliases once, then fall back to stub_record; APIError, refusal, or max_tokens stop -> stub the whole batch and record the failure; never raise. The API is a true external, so a fake client is acceptable for behavior tests. Unverified and to prototype later: whether Anthropic's recommended tool_result delivery composes with structured outputs.

tasks.title: Prompt-injection regression tests over synthetic hostile email
tasks.notes: test-only: the product is the regression suite; there is no production symbol to grep. Synthetic fixtures only (public repo). Cases: body containing </document> and 'ignore previous instructions'; HTML with display:none / hidden instructions (must be absent from the built request, end to end: raw Gmail fixture -> flatten_message -> normalize -> build_request); a fake model reply whose one_line carries a URL and a canary string (URL must be stripped, alias to unknown id dropped); request has no tools key; system prompt contains the untrusted-content policy. Run injection-resistance assertions across several fake replies (pass^k style: all must hold), never assert exact LLM text (Sonnet-class output is not reproducible).

tasks.title: pipeline.triage_cli: dry-run the map call over collected Gmail items

runs.tail:
usage: triage_cli.py [-h] [--hours HOURS] [--limit LIMIT]
                     [--batch-size BATCH_SIZE] [--dry]
                     source

Run the triage map call over collected Gmail items. Writes nothing.

positional arguments:
  source                stored source id, e.g. gmail_personal

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --hours HOURS         lookback window (default 24)
  --limit LIMIT         records to print (default 5)
  --batch-size BATCH_SIZE
                        items per call (default 20)
  --dry                 print the first request only: no API key, no network

tasks.notes: Mirrors pipeline/collect.py: python -m pipeline.triage_cli <source> [--hours N] [--limit N] [--dry]. Reads CollectedItem rows for the source within the window (add a small db helper such as items_for_source_since(source, since); items_for_run exists but is per-run), normalizes them, and with --dry prints the batched request JSON WITHOUT calling the API and without any API key; without --dry it calls triage_items and prints each record with its source alias. Writes NOTHING to the database. This is how the map step is judged against real Gmail data; the live call is a manual step that spends API credit.

tasks.title: Send participant roles to the triage model; drop the httpx2 import from tests
tasks.notes: Found in T-012 review. build_request sent participants as bare 'Name <addr>' strings, so the model cannot tell the sender from recipients, which matters for judging action_needed (asked of the reader?). Add a helper _participant_line(participant) -> str that renders '<role>: Name <addr>' (role is from|to|cc; omit '<>' when there is no display name and no angle brackets when there is no name), used for each item's participants list; the field name and the rest of the request shape do not change. Update the tests that assert the participant format and add a case with all three roles and a nameless address. Also replace the direct 'import httpx2' in tests/test_triage_client.py with a small stand-in request object (anthropic.APIConnectionError only stores the request) so the test suite does not depend on the SDK's transitive HTTP library; the contract test against the real Messages.parse signature must remain.

tasks.title: Harden sanitize_text: strip other URI schemes and protocol-relative links
tasks.notes: Found in T-013 review. sanitize_text (pipeline/triage.py, _URL) strips only http(s):// and www. forms; a hostile or confused model reply can still carry ftp://, mailto:, javascript:, data:, file:, tel: URIs or protocol-relative //host/path into the digest, which is later rendered to PDF. Extend the URL removal to those schemes (case-insensitive, also when written with odd spacing is NOT required) and to //host/path forms, removing them the same way existing URLs are removed. Do NOT strip bare domains (evil.example.net, Acme.com): false positives on company names and file names outweigh the gain for a PDF digest; say so in a comment. Keep the existing behavior for markdown links (label kept, target dropped). Add tests to tests/test_triage.py for each new scheme (in plain text and as a markdown link target), for //host, for a bare domain being left alone, and for a sentence where removal leaves no double spaces. The existing 62 triage tests and the injection suite must keep passing unchanged.
